Treasure graph

What each of Wario Land 3's 100 treasures needs, and the earliest point it can be taken. The main line (48 treasures, down the left) is the Gold Music Box and everything it needs, in the order the Temple hint gives them. The other 52 are branches: each one is drawn at the last main-line treasure it needs, so that's where it becomes available, often long before the hint asks for it (the hint's number is on each chip).

Tap a treasure: what it needs lights up in orange, what it opens in green, and the panel says why, with sources. Back to the treasure map page.

To check in the game (5)

Uncertain needs, needs that rest on the heuristic alone, and places where sources disagree. The same list is on the review page; answers go in tools/treasure_requirements.json.

  • W1 blue chest, hint #37. Now: needs Super Jump Slam Overalls (heuristic (power-up map flash + lowest chest)). Why: an edge comes only from the heuristic.
    • game data: the Super Jump Slam Overalls flash Desert Ruins
    • heuristic (power-up map flash + lowest chest): grey and red are open from the start and the green needs the Head Smash Helmet (Super Mario Wiki), so the blue one is the chest the overalls open
    • Super Mario Wiki: Desert Ruins: the blue chest is under Yellow Belly, beaten with Smash Attacks on its head

    Check: Can the blue chest of W1 (Sun Medallion Bottom) be reached without the Super Jump Slam Overalls?

  • W2 red chest, hint #51. Now: needs Truck Wheel (guide), Flute (game data). Why: sources missing or not conclusive.
    • Super Mario Wiki: The Volcano's Base: the carts run once the Truck Wheel is fitted; the ride ends at a platform with a door and a snake pot
    • game data: the cart checks TRUCK_WHEEL itself (CartVariableFunc); the Flute switches The Volcano's Base to variant 3, new room headers

    Check: Can the red chest of W2 (Blue Gem) be reached without the Truck Wheel? Can the red chest of W2 (Blue Gem) be reached without the Flute? With the Truck Wheel but before the Flute (and before the Foot of Stone): does the cart reach the red key and chest?

  • N2 green chest, hint #53. Now: needs nothing besides the level. Why: sources missing or not conclusive.
    • Super Mario Wiki: The Peaceful Village: the door to the Goblet only opens at night; by day Wario needs the Super Jump Slam Overalls (or the High Jump Boots) for a secret entrance
    • game data: variant 1 has its own night block map (.the_peaceful_village_2); from the Flute on, night uses the day map; the Super Jump Slam Overalls flash the village

    Check: Can the green chest of N2 (Goblet) be reached as soon as N2 opens, with no power-up, by day and by night? Is the Goblet's night-only door still there after the Flute (from then on the village loads variants 2-4, which use the day block map at night too)? If not, it needs the Super Jump Slam Overalls.

  • W2 green chest, hint #54. Now: needs Truck Wheel (guide), Flute (game data). Why: sources missing or not conclusive.
    • Super Mario Wiki: The Volcano's Base: the Crown's key and chest are in the upper part of the mountain, reached with the carts
    • game data: as for the Blue Gem

    Check: Can the green chest of W2 (Crown) be reached without the Truck Wheel? Can the green chest of W2 (Crown) be reached without the Flute? With the Truck Wheel but before the Flute (and before the Foot of Stone): does the cart reach the green key and chest?

  • E7 green chest, hint #68. Now: needs Mystery Handle (game data). Why: sources missing or not conclusive.
    • game data: the Mystery Handle raises a pipe and switches Forest of Fear to variant 3; the green chest is hinted right after it
    • Super Mario Wiki: Forest of Fear: the raised pipe is next to the grey chest

    Check: Can the green chest of E7 (Warp Removal Apparatus) be reached without the Mystery Handle? Before the Mystery Handle: is there any way to the green key and chest?

Where the needs come from: 56 treasures have a guide that says it and game data that agrees, 40 come from the game data alone, 4 are uncertain. Level openings are always game data. Edges by source: game data (level open): 140, guide: 62, game data: 19, verified in game by Taro: 2, heuristic (power-up map flash + lowest chest): 1. The heuristic (a power-up flashes a level on the map: it opens the lowest-colour chest there that can't be taken yet) agrees with the requirements for 23 of 24 power-up flashes.
